ruling.recommended_action: Refund SGD 3.34 (excess distance fare for the 4.22 km deviation) to the rider's original payment method; issue the driver a notification-duty reminder and log the uninformed reroute on his route-compliance record (no formal warning — first such incident); no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
Deviation (RD-1): actual 17.55 km − recommended 13.329 km = 4.221 km, well over the 1 km tolerance. The GPS shows the driver left the recommended corridor at ~09:06–09:07 (Kaki Bukit Road 2 / Avenue 2 → Eunos Link → Jalan Eunos) and rejoined at Paya Lebar Road (~09:14), i.e. one off-route segment of about 4.2 km. This is not map-matching noise and the deviation must be checked under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5.

Consent and the named road (RD-3 / RD-5): the chat shows the driver asked "can I go round via Ubi Avenue 2?" at 09:03:00 and the rider answered "Sure, no problem." at 09:03:40 — before the deviation began. Consent is tied to the road the rider was asked about. Ubi Avenue 2 does not appear anywhere on the road actually driven (COMPASSVALE CRESCENT/ROAD, SENGKANG SQUARE, SENGKANG EAST AVENUE/DRIVE, BUANGKOK EAST DRIVE, KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY, KAKI BUKIT ROAD 2, KAKI BUKIT AVENUE 2, EUNOS LINK, JALAN EUNOS, CHANGI ROAD, GEYLANG SERAI, GEYLANG ROAD, PAYA LEBAR ROAD, CIRCUIT LINK, PIPIT ROAD, NICOLL UNDERPASS/HIGHWAY, STADIUM DRIVE/PLACE). Under RD-5 the segment only falls inside the rider's consent if the named road is present; it is absent, so the consent does not cover it. The driver's own statement confirms he deliberately went "by Jalan Eunos instead because it looked clearer" — his own convenience, not the route the rider agreed to. Accordingly the segment counts as an off-route deviation, not exempt.

Traffic reason (RD-4): the only traffic band on the recommended route, KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY (speed band 2, ~08:48–09:16), ends at 09:16:50; the deviation ran ~09:06–09:07 (the last KPE sample before turning off is 09:06:20 at 15.0 km/h), i.e. it began only after the band had expired, so no traffic exemption attaches at that time. In any event RD-4 never exempts a segment; with no traffic justification RD-2 gives a partial refund of the excess distance fare and a driver violation is recorded.

Amount (RD-2): this trip's per-km distance fare = 24.75 / 17.55 = $1.410/km. Refundable km = 4.221 km deviation − 0 km exempt = 4.22 km. Refund = 4.22 × 1.410 = $3.34 (tolls 0, time fare and the 1.0× surge are not refunded).

Safety screen: the chat, driver statement and complaint contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — nothing to escalate. The $3.34 is under $10, so under TH-1 (and DISP-001, C1) the system rules finally. Precedents PREC-1: DISP-2026-0089 (uninformed reroute → partial refund of excess distance fare) is on point; DISP-2026-0142 (surge) and DISP-2026-0211 (no-show) do not apply.

Rider flag: no rider issue — do not flag. Driver flag (RD-6): the driver's last-90-day record has one upheld dispute but zero route_deviation_upheld_against, so the 90-day route-deviation repeat condition is not met and no flag_account is applied.

segment_findings.reason: Consent chat at 09:03 was expressly conditioned on going via Ubi Avenue 2 (RD-5); the GPS shows the segment instead drove Kaki Bukit Road 2 / Kaki Bukit Avenue 2 / Eunos Link / Jalan Eunos, and Ubi Avenue 2 appears nowhere on the segment, so the named-road consent does not cover it. The driver's statement confirms he chose Jalan Eunos for his own convenience ('it looked clearer'), which is not the agreed route (RD-3). The only relevant traffic band (KPE, band 2) had expired before the segment began, and in any case a traffic reason never exempts a segment (RD-4). Segment therefore counts; exempt km = 0 (RD-2).

A residual ~0.02–0.06 km unallocated gap remains after the identified off-route segment against the 4.221 km total deviation, entirely within 10–60 m of map-matching noise on connected roads; at the trip rate this is under $0.09 and is not independently refundable (RD-1 system detail: departures under 0.2 km are noise). Noted for completeness.

element_findings.element: RD-5 rider consent to a specific named road (Ubi Avenue 2) before/at the start of the deviation
element_findings.reason: Driver chat 09:03:00 'can I go round via Ubi Avenue 2?', rider 09:03:40 'Sure, no problem.' — a clear pre-segment agreement to go via the named road.

element_findings.element: RD-5 road-name check: was the consented road (Ubi Avenue 2) present on the segment driven
element_findings.reason: No telemetry sample on the off-route segment (Kaki Bukit Road 2, Kaki Bukit Avenue 2, Eunos Link, Jalan Eunos) is Ubi Avenue 2, and the driver admits he went by Jalan Eunos instead; the consent is therefore untied to the road driven and does not exempt the segment.

element_findings.element: RD-4 traffic reason attaching to the segment
element_findings.reason: The sole congestion record (KALLANG PAYA LEBAR EXPRESSWAY, speed band 2) runs 08:48:20–09:16:50 on the recommended route, but the deviation began ~09:06–09:07 (last KPE sample 09:06:20, 15 km/h) at a point where the band had ended; no closure/incident within 300 m is recorded, so no traffic exemption applies.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver's claim that 'the rider agreed' does not exempt the segment: consent was to a specific named road (Ubi Avenue 2) that he did not drive, and he states himself he went by Jalan Eunos 'because it looked clearer' — a driver-chosen route, not the agreed one (RD-5 / RD-3). Verbal-claim characterisation of the agreement is a claim, not consent.

His further claim 'same direction' / clear roads is not a traffic justification: no qualifying closure, incident or congestion band (1–2) is recorded on the replaced part of the recommended route during the deviation (RD-4), and a traffic reason would not exempt the segment in any case.
